title: kuberecord — Namespace Activity
description: Where the cluster is moving. A heatmap of change volume by namespace over time, with the breakdowns needed to explain a hot cell: which event types, which kinds, and which namespaces carry the volume. Use it to spot the deploy nobody announced, the namespace that never goes quiet, and the retention cost you are about to pay.

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: The ClickHouse holding kuberecord's resource_states table.

list.name: cluster
list.label: Cluster
list.description: cluster_id is the leading column of the sort key, so every panel filters on it.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT cluster_id FROM resource_states ORDER BY cluster_id

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT cluster_id FROM resource_states ORDER BY cluster_id

list.name: kind
list.label: Kind
list.description: Multi-select, All by default. Restricting to the kinds you deploy — Deployment, ConfigMap, Ingress — turns 'activity' into 'deploys' by filtering out the status churn of controller-owned kinds.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT kind FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY kind

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT kind FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY kind

list.name: event_type
list.label: Event type
list.description: The event types to count. The list is the frozen schema's state machine, written out rather than queried, so the options stay stable even in a window where one of them happens not to occur. Snapshot marks a row written while the operator was still warming and could not know whether the object was new; Checkpoint is a Modified that also carries full state.

panels.title: Change volume by namespace
panels.description: One row per namespace, one cell per time bucket, coloured by how many rows kuberecord wrote. Cluster-scoped objects have an empty namespace in the schema and are shown as (cluster-scoped) so they do not render as a nameless row. Bucketing follows the dashboard's interval, so widening the time range coarsens the cells rather than dropping data.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
    if(namespace = '', '(cluster-scoped)', namespace) AS ns,
    count() AS changes
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND kind IN (${kind:sqlstring})
  AND event_type IN (${event_type:sqlstring})
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY time, ns
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Change volume by event type
panels.description: The same volume, split by what kind of change it was. The mix is the diagnosis: a wall of Modified is churn, a step of Added is a rollout, a burst of Deleted is a teardown, and a spike of Snapshot means the operator restarted and re-baselined rather than that anything happened in the cluster.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
    event_type,
    count() AS changes
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND kind IN (${kind:sqlstring})
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY time, event_type
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Kinds by volume
panels.description: Which kinds are producing the rows, group-qualified because a kind name alone is ambiguous once CRDs are in play. This is the panel to read before widening a rule: a kind near the top of this list will dominate storage, and a kind absent from it is being watched for nothing.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    concat(if(api_group = '', 'core', api_group), '/', kind) AS gvk,
    count()                        AS changes,
    uniqExact((namespace, name))   AS objects,
    max(ts)                        AS last_change
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND event_type IN (${event_type:sqlstring})
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY gvk
ORDER BY changes DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Busiest namespaces
panels.description: The heatmap as numbers, with the event-type split per namespace and the number of distinct objects behind the volume. The ratio of the two is the useful bit: many rows over few objects is churn to investigate on the Flap Report, while many rows over many objects is simply a busy namespace.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    if(namespace = '', '(cluster-scoped)', namespace) AS ns,
    countIf(event_type = 'Added')                    AS added,
    countIf(event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')) AS modified,
    countIf(event_type = 'Deleted')                  AS deleted,
    countIf(event_type = 'Snapshot')                 AS snapshot,
    count()                                          AS total,
    uniqExact((api_group, kind, name))               AS objects
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND kind IN (${kind:sqlstring})
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY ns
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 50
